contexts.WH: Whether it proved to be a winner or not, investors had gathered around it, and they were rapidly gaining funds.
contexts.MG: Whether it would prove to be a winner or not, investors had gathered around it, and they were rapidly gaining funds.
contexts.UP: Investors were gathering, jumping on the bandwagon of their own accord, and the business was rapidly gathering funds.

MG.japanese: 確かに蔵臼が豪語した事業は、この一年でさらに規模が大きくなり、当初の見込みを大幅に上回る利益を約束しつつあった。勝ち馬には放って置いても出資者が集まり、資金が見る見る集まる。カネがカネを呼ぶとはまさにこのことだろう。
MG.translation: Certainly, this business Krauss boasted of had expanded in scope over the last year... and was promising an even greater payoff than had been anticipated initially. Whether it would prove to be a winner or not, investors had gathered around it, and they were rapidly gaining funds. This must be what they mean when they say money summons money.

UP.japanese: 確かに蔵臼が豪語した事業は、この一年でさらに規模が大きくなり、当初の見込みを大幅に上回る利益を約束しつつあった。勝ち馬には放って置いても出資者が集まり、資金が見る見る集まる。カネがカネを呼ぶとはまさにこのことだろう。
UP.translation: Certainly, this business Krauss boasted of had expanded in scope over the last year, and was promising an even greater payoff than had been anticipated in the beginning. Investors were gathering, jumping on the bandwagon of their own accord, and the business was rapidly gathering funds. It was a perfect example of the saying "money makes money".

findings.sourceReading: 勝ち馬には放って置いても means investors gather around a winning horse even when left alone. The winning prospect explains the self-reinforcing influx of funds.
findings.alternative: The next money-summons-money sentence preserves self-reinforcement, but whether it proved a winner or not replaces the source’s condition with indifference to success.

findings.description: A small setback to good fortune becomes taking fortune for granted.

contexts.japanese: 確かに、運気というのは小さなケチで転ぶこともある。
contexts.japanesePC: 確かに、運気というのは小さなケチで転ぶこともある。
contexts.japanesePS3: 確かに、運気というのは小さなケチで転ぶこともある。
contexts.WH: Certainly, fortune tends to turn against people who take it for granted even in the slightest.
contexts.MG: Certainly, fortune tends to turn against people who take it for granted even in the slightest.
contexts.UP: Certainly, fortune tends to turn against people who take it for granted even in the slightest.

MG.japanese:
確かに、運気というのは小さなケチで転ぶこともある。
急いては事を何とやら……。蔵臼はこれまで、じっくり待てば必ず利益が上げられた事業を、いくつも焦って清算し、自ら勝ち馬を降りるような真似をしてきた。
MG.translation: Certainly, fortune tends to turn against people who take it for granted even in the slightest. Anxious beggars never prosper... On many occasions before now, Krauss had gotten cold feet and sold off businesses that would surely have brought in a profit had he just waited, and had, in effect, given away his winning picks.

UP.japanese:
確かに、運気というのは小さなケチで転ぶこともある。
急いては事を何とやら……。蔵臼はこれまで、じっくり待てば必ず利益が上げられた事業を、いくつも焦って清算し、自ら勝ち馬を降りるような真似をしてきた。
UP.translation:
Certainly, fortune tends to turn against people who take it for granted even in the slightest.
There's a saying about hasty anglers...... On many occasions before now, Krauss had gotten cold feet and sold businesses that would surely have brought in a profit had he just waited, and had, in effect, given away his winning picks.

findings.sourceReading: 小さなケチ here is a small adverse incident or snag that can turn the course of good fortune. This follows concern that unusual fundraising might create mistrust.
findings.alternative: The surrounding caution could loosely support a moral warning, but the Japanese does not identify complacency or taking good luck for granted as the cause.

MG.translation: That's right. I already know how I can reach the end of that journey. It's been made clear to me since the very beginning.

findings.sourceReading: そして最初から、それを掲げている continues Battler as subject: he has upheld/proclaimed the method. MG adds to me to the passive, turning him into its recipient; PC12113–12114 has passive shown without that added recipient. UP restores active proclamation.
findings.alternative: Knowing the method is stated in190, but191 is a separate claim about his displaying it; made clear to me changes that predicate and agent.

findings.description: UP broadens Natsuhi's prohibition on suspicious contacts into a prohibition on connections with other men.

contexts.japanese: 妻たるもの、夫以外の、それも若い男性と、疑われるような接点があるべきではない。
contexts.japanesePS3: 妻たるもの、夫以外の、それも若い男性と、疑われるような接点があるべきではない。
contexts.MG: As a wife, she must avoid any contact that might be considered suspicious with anyone other than her husband, much less a young man.
contexts.UP: Natsuhi thought that as a wife, it wasn't right for her to have connections with men other than her husband, much less a young man; it might be considered suspicious.

MG.japanese: 妻たるもの、夫以外の、それも若い男性と、疑われるような接点があるべきではない。そう思うと、急に汚らわしい電話のように思えてきた。
MG.translation: As a wife, she must avoid any contact that might be considered suspicious with anyone other than her husband, much less a young man. As soon as she thought this, the phone call suddenly seemed like something dirty.

UP.japanese: 妻たるもの、夫以外の、それも若い男性と、疑われるような接点があるべきではない。そう思うと、急に汚らわしい電話のように思えてきた。
UP.translation: Natsuhi thought that as a wife, it wasn't right for her to have connections with men other than her husband, much less a young man; it might be considered suspicious. The phone call suddenly seemed like something dirty.

findings.sourceReading: 疑われるような接点 restricts the forbidden contacts to ones inviting suspicion. UP prohibits connections with men other than her husband and then gives suspicion as a reason. PC12882–12884 and MG retain the restricted scope.
findings.alternative: Suspicion remains an explicit reason, but the semicolon clause does not restrict the preceding categorical prohibition to suspicious connections.

findings.description: PC 慌てる乞食は何とやら uses the beggar proverb. Maintained PS3 JP 急いては事を何とやら uses the haste proverb. MG Anxious beggars never prosper preserves the PC reference.

contexts.japanese: 急いては事を何とやら……。
contexts.japanesePC: 慌てる乞食は何とやら......。
contexts.japanesePS3: 急いては事を何とやら……。
contexts.WH: Like by anxiously begging for money......
contexts.MG: Anxious beggars never prosper...
contexts.UP: There's a saying about hasty anglers......

MG.japanese:
確かに、運気というのは小さなケチで転ぶこともある。
急いては事を何とやら……。蔵臼はこれまで、じっくり待てば必ず利益が上げられた事業を、いくつも焦って清算し、自ら勝ち馬を降りるような真似をしてきた。
MG.translation: Certainly, fortune tends to turn against people who take it for granted even in the slightest. Anxious beggars never prosper... On many occasions before now, Krauss had gotten cold feet and sold off businesses that would surely have brought in a profit had he just waited, and had, in effect, given away his winning picks.

UP.japanese:
確かに、運気というのは小さなケチで転ぶこともある。
急いては事を何とやら……。蔵臼はこれまで、じっくり待てば必ず利益が上げられた事業を、いくつも焦って清算し、自ら勝ち馬を降りるような真似をしてきた。
UP.translation:
Certainly, fortune tends to turn against people who take it for granted even in the slightest.
There's a saying about hasty anglers...... On many occasions before now, Krauss had gotten cold feet and sold businesses that would surely have brought in a profit had he just waited, and had, in effect, given away his winning picks.
